<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In order to prepare for possible future operation of JT-60SA with tungsten plasma facing components, a H-mode scenario of JT-60SA at high power and high current is considered as reference in order to investigate the tungsten transport behaviour and assess the amount of electron cyclotron resonance heating (ECRH) which is predicted to be required in order to avoid central accumulation of tungsten. The modelling is performed with the ASTRA transport code in combination with the TGLF-SAT2 quasi-linear turbulent transport model and with neoclassical transport of impurities computed by the drift-kinetic solver NEO and the FACIT model. The impact of argon as additional seeded impurity is also considered, not only in the core behavior but also on the possibility of achieving tungsten screening in the pedestal region. The main result is that these H-mode conditions in JT-60SA achieve a so far largely unexplored domain of parameters, in which a reactor-like very low collisionality is combined with high rotation levels. In contrast to the usual domain of operation of present medium size tokamaks, where tungsten neoclassical transport is in the plateau to Pfirsch-Schlüter regime, in the predicted JT-60SA conditions toroidal rotation has a beneficial effect in increasing the strength of the temperature screening, enabling operation without any strong central tungsten accumulation and, in the most unfavorable conditions of high tungsten concentration and low rotation, requiring only 2 MW of central ECRH power to avoid locally negative electron heat fluxes in the center. Within the limited predictive capabilities of the present modelling approach for pedestal parameters, a sufficiently large and realistic domain of parameters in terms of argon concentration and plasma rotation, as well as of relative density and temperature logarithmic gradients, can also be expected to lead to the dominance of tungsten temperature screening in the JT-60SA pedestal.</jats:p>
title_ko: 고출력 고전류 JT-60SA H-모드 플라즈마에서의 텅스텐 거동 예측

title: Implementation and application of a runaway electron impact module in HEAT
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Runaway electrons (REs) are relativistic particles which can cause damage to plasma facing components (PFCs) in tokamaks. It is essential to study the damage to PFCs from RE impacts in future devices, due to their higher plasma currents and therefor higher potential for damage. In order to do this, a novel RE module has been added to the HEAT code, and the methods used in this code are described in this paper. This module builds on existing physics in HEAT such as magnetic field line following, PFC CAD meshing, and heat flux calculations, but adds in relativistic effects, drifts, and tracking through time-varying equilibria in order to better capture the dynamics of REs. Simulations take in parameters of the RE beam such as energies, pitch angles, and initial positions for the electrons as well as the total current of the beam. The simulation outputs RE trajectories and heat fluxes on the relevant PFC geometry. The RE module is used to analyze Alcator C-Mod discharge&#xD;1080326005 during which REs melted a diagnostic cable. HEAT simulations using axisymmetric magnetic reconstructions find a heat flux pattern that closely matches the damage pattern on the cables themselves, thereby demonstrating the capabilities and value of this new module.</jats:p>
title_ko: HEAT에 런어웨이 전자 충돌 모듈 구현 및 적용

title: Effect of plasma beta on the access to marginal suppression of type-I ELMs with n = 4 resonant magnetic perturbations in EAST
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We present experimental observations of marginal suppression of large Type-I Edge Localized Modes (ELMs) using $n = 4$ Resonant Magnetic Perturbations (RMPs) in the EAST tokamak, with energy confinement maintained.&#xD;The edge safety factor and the normalized plasma beta are relevant to the ITER baseline scenario, $q_{95}\approx3.1$ and $\beta_N\approx1.8$--$2.0$.&#xD;Marginal ELM suppression was observed when $\beta_N$ exceeded 1.8, with tungsten divertors and low recycling conditions.&#xD;To investigate the underlying mechanism, quasi-linear modeling is performed, revealing that an increased plasma beta enhances the plasma response and the associated neoclassical toroidal viscosity (NTV) torque, reducing the RMP coil current required for field penetration.&#xD;The findings suggest that increasing $\beta_N$ facilitates the transition from ELMy H-mode to marginal ELM suppression, which is favourable for ELM control with high-$n$ RMPs in future fusion devices, including ITER.</jats:p>
title_ko: EAST에서 n = 4 공진 자기섭동을 이용한 Type-I ELM의 한계 억제에 대한 플라즈마 베타(plasma beta)의 영향

title: Advanced computational methodologies for water activation assessment and applications to JET
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    In water-cooled D-T fusion tokamaks, such as the Joint European Torus (JET), neutron activation of flowing water generates short-lived radionuclides (
                    <jats:sup>16</jats:sup>
                    N,
                    <jats:sup>17</jats:sup>
                    N and
                    <jats:sup>19</jats:sup>
                    O), producing a distributed source of high-energy gamma radiation and delayed neutrons. The energy and intensity of the source are driving factors in the design of cooling and shielding systems and, if not understood early in the design, can lead to significantly increased costs. While several past and future experiments provide fusion-relevant water activation benchmarking data, the JET water circuit is the first to use a fusion tokamak environment. This provides a unique opportunity to benchmark fluid activation codes for applicability to ITER and other fusion devices, with a relevant deuterium-tritium (D-T) 14 MeV neutron spectrum, and a large water-cooling pipe network. The part of the network monitored includes the neutral beam injector (NBI) duct scraper and cooling for the rotary high vacuum valve (RHVV), which forms part of the same duct. Several computational tools have been developed in order to calculate the activation of moving fluids in fusion environments. These utilise a variety of approaches to couple neutron activation, fluid dynamics and radiation transport. The JET water circuit poses a challenge to tools which utilise computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations to replicate the transport of water through a system. This manuscript details the analysis of the JET cooling circuit with the GammaFlow code and the comparison with experimental results. It is found that the code is able to reproduce the water travel time and detector pulse shape with reasonable accuracy. The activity concentration of
                    <jats:sup>16</jats:sup>
                    N is calculated with an average C/E=0.9
                    <jats:sub>-0.3</jats:sub>
                    <jats:sup>+0.2</jats:sup>
                    for the pulses evaluated. This is an important benchmark analysis demonstrating that fluid activation codes are capable of accurate predictions of radiation dose maps for future water-cooled fusion devices.

title: Co-occurrence of Elevated Natural Radioactivity and Potentially Toxic Elements in Laboni Beach Sands: Source Provenance and Radiological Hazards Assessment
abstract: This study first reported high levels of naturally occurring radionuclides 226Ra (460 Bq/kg) and 232Th (838 Bq/kg) in Laboni Beach, compared to world average and other coastal beaches in Bangladesh. Twenty-five sand samples were collected to determine natural radionuclides (226Ra, 232Th and 40K) using the HPGe gamma spectrometry. To understand the origin of radioactive sources, the elements of heavy metals meticulously studied by FAAS absorption spectrophotometer and ICP-OES optical emission spectroscopy, where Fe, Mn, Cr, Cd, As, Sb, and Se were found to be 1.48, 1.15, 2.25, 29.3, 1.29, 1.9, and 5.54 times higher than the earth’s continental crust values. The co-occurrence of natural radionuclides (226Ra and 232Th) with Pb, Cu, Cd, and Fe suggests their enrichment from a common geogenic source through heavy mineral concentration. Elevated 232Th/226Ra (mean: 1.85, 2.2 × world average), 232Th/40K (mean: 4.02, 57.4 × world average), and 226Ra/40K (mean: 2.21, 2.5 × world average) ratios, corroborated by statistical analyses and source apportionment model, confirm the predominance of Th-rich heavy-mineral assemblages and their control on the enrichment of natural radionuclides and associated heavy metals. The predominance of Cadmium (Cd) and Chromium (Cr) in the ecological risk index identifies as the principal ecological risk factors. Radiological health risk evaluation demonstrated that all hazard indices exceeded the recommended safety limits, underscoring significant public health concerns for local residents, tourists, and the use of beach sands as construction materials.

title: Assessment of the 3D Pressure Drop Tensor Formulation in Porous Media for Tube Bundle Configurations
abstract: Porous media modeling is often retained in the nuclear industry for the thermal-hydraulics component scale simulation of the core and of steam generators. In this approach, the fuel/tube bundle solid boundaries are not explicitly simulated, and their presence is modeled by a volume porosity and a pressure drop source term in the momentum equations, the goal of which is to describe the forces induced by the structures on the flow. This paper attempts to assess the consistency of the pressure drop formulation in 3D cylinder bundle configurations. The first part of the paper describes the possible tensor formulations and proposes a simple test case to show potential weaknesses in reproducing experimental data. For the tensor formulations tested, it was not possible to obtain the pressure drop corresponding to the correlation value, for angles of the flow different than 0 and 90 deg with respect to the tube direction. In the second part of the paper, a 3D external single-phase flow across an oblique tube bundle is considered: the tube bundle is made of 20 × 20 triangular-pitch straight tubes, with a 45-deg angle between the tubes and the free stream. This configuration was simulated through both a porous media and a computational fluid dynamics (CFD) approach (RANS). CFD results are averaged along control volumes representative of the porous media simulation scale. The velocity profiles calculated by the two approaches are compared along different profiles inside the tube bundle: regions with different flow deviation predicted by the two approaches are identified.

title: Transport due to density gradient driven TEM & UM in advanced tokamak plasma configurations: Role of negative triangularity and magnetic shear reversal
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Advanced tokamak configurations can modify microturbulence through changes in magnetic equilibrium, trapped-particle dynamics, resonance conditions. In this work, global gyrokinetic simulations are used to study density-gradient-driven trapped-electron turbulence in tight-aspect-ratio shaped plasmas, focusing on the role of negative triangularity and reversed magnetic shear. In the positive versus negative triangularity comparison, negative triangularity is found to stabilize high-n modes and reduce saturated particle diffusivity by approximately 40%. Energy-exchange diagnostics show that this reduction is associated with a weaker participation of weakly trapped electrons, while zonal-flow shearing remains comparable between the two configurations. In the reversed-shear case for positive triangularity, despite larger linear growth rates, the saturated electron diffusivity is reduced by approximately 36% as compared to positive magnetic shear case. This reduction is linked to the diminished radial support of the perturbation in the negative magnetic-shear region. The combined effect of reversed magnetic shear and negative triangularity is further investigated, revealing that although both independently reduce saturated transport levels, their combination leads to enhanced nonlinear transport.</jats:p>

title: Recent achievements at the ITER Neutral Beam Test Facility, and mission within the ITER research plan
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The Heating and Current Drive Neutral Beam Injectors in ITER will be essential in the DT phase to reach burning plasma condition and control advanced scenarios, providing at least 33 MW of heating power by neutral beams of hydrogen (0.87 MeV) or deuterium (1 MeV).&#xD;The operation of a full-scale negative ion source (SPIDER) and a complete injector prototype&#xD;(MITICA) are being validated at the Neutral Beam Test Facility (NBTF) in Padova, Italy,&#xD;within a long-term strategy integrated with the revised ITER Research Plan. Following its&#xD;first major shutdown, SPIDER completed a validation campaign (SO-2), operating 320&#xD;beamlets simultaneously for the first time, reaching ⁓700 kW beam power and an extracted&#xD;current density of 215 A/m2 in hydrogen at 0.3 Pa and RF power of 72 kW/driver – in line&#xD;with the scaling towards ITER target – together with a substantial increase in pulse duration.&#xD;Meanwhile, MITICA completed a dedicated campaign on high voltage insulation in vacuum,&#xD;demonstrating equivalent voltage holding up to 910 kV at HNB-relevant pressure using an&#xD;intermediate electrostatic shield, a result directly relevant to the 870 kV target. The&#xD;restoration and improvement process of the MITICA power supply, damaged during the first&#xD;integrated tests, is in its final phase ahead of the repetition of the full integrated tests.</jats:p>

title: On the feasibility of model-based regulation of vertical instability growth rate using out-vessel coils in ARC-like scenarios
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In this work, we propose a model-based feedback controller that regulates the vertical instability growth rate (γgr )&#xD;of a high-elongation, double-null tokamak directly, using only out-vessel poloidal field (PF) coils. High elongation&#xD;raises the achievable plasma current and fusion performance but makes the plasma vertically unstable, and in a&#xD;fusion power plant the in-vessel coils that present devices rely on for stabilization may be absent, leaving only&#xD;distant out-vessel circuits. The controller couples a machine learning surrogate of non-rigid, profile agnostic vertical&#xD;instability metric to a constrained quadratic program: the surrogate supplies real-time γgr estimates and, via&#xD;automatic differentiation, the actuator sensitivities, while the program allocates coil voltages to track a target&#xD;growth rate, maintain double-null divertor balance, and respect electromechanical limits. We tested this method on&#xD;the ARC V3A power plant design configuration across 24 closed-loop simulations spanning equilibrium variations,&#xD;actuator degradations, and transient disturbances. We achieved full or marginal success in 83% of these cases&#xD;(full in 50%, marginal in a further 33%) and lose control in the remaining 17%; the failures map the boundary of&#xD;out-vessel controllability (occurring at the highest growth rates) and under actuator limits. The controller does&#xD;not regulate boundary shape explicitly: separatrix geometry follows indirectly from growth rate and flux balance&#xD;control and would require a separate shape control layer for sustained scenario evolution.</jats:p>
title_ko: ARC 유사 시나리오에서 외부 코일을 사용하여 수직 불안정성 증가율을 모델 기반으로 제어하는 것의 타당성

title: Behavior of kinetic instabilities in a dynamically forming resonant distribution
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Instabilities driven by energetic particles are central to the physics of a burning plasma. The majority of kinetic simulations and reduced models assume that the unstable distribution is already fully established when energetic-particle-driven modes grow unstable. In realistic scenarios, however, energetic particles may accumulate in the resonance on an effective timescale comparable to the growth rate of the instability, meaning that the formation of the resonant distribution and the growth of the unstable mode must be treated concurrently. We study the behavior of these instabilities in the presence of such a dynamically forming distribution, evaluating two distinct metrics which measure how close a mode is to its linear stability threshold and how close a mode remains to its nonlinear stability threshold. It is found that saturation at large $\omega_b/\nu_\text{eff}$ (where $\omega_b$ is the bounce frequency of deeply trapped particles and $\nu_\text{eff}$ is the effective scattering rate at a resonance), normally associated with strongly driven excitation, can be achieved even if dynamically the mode remains at all times near its nonlinear stability threshold. We extend existing analytic models for near-marginal and far from marginal modes allowing for a time-dependent linear growth rate, deriving explicit expressions for the mode amplitude evolution. These formulas are shown to agree with nonlinear kinetic simulations.  The discrepancies between the case of a dynamically forming distribution and the case of a fully formed distribution are shown to be particularly pronounced for energetic particle distributions which relax diffusively. We interpret these results in the context of realistic experimental parameters, and propose an experimentally measurable figure of merit for a mode's proximity to nonlinear threshold.</jats:p>
title_ko: 동적으로 형성되는 공진 분포에서 운동 불안정성의 거동

title: 3D modelling of runaway electron deconfinement by MHD instabilities in ITER mitigated disruptions: from avalanche to termination
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The effect of MHD instabilities on runaway electron (RE) avalanche and termination in ITER mitigated disruptions is investigated using MHD simulations with the JOREK code. 3D simulations show that the MHD stability during the current quench (CQ) is highly sensitive to the density profile and the initial current profile after the thermal quench. The impurity and electron density distributions play a dominant role by influencing the temperature and current-density profiles during the CQ. In the most unstable simulation case with high edge density and sufficient edge cooling, magnetic field lines stay globally stochastic for more than 10 ms, substantially reducing the peak RE current to kA level in the baseline simulation. To assess uncertainty in the diffusion-based fluid RE transport model, the parallel diffusivity is reduced from 10
                    <jats:sup>10</jats:sup>
                    to 10
                    <jats:sup>9</jats:sup>
                    m
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    s
                    <jats:sup>-1</jats:sup>
                    in a reference case, giving an upper-limit estimate of 0.57 MA for the peak RE current. Due to limited diagnostic data during disruptions, the link between the current profile and CQ MHD activity has not been tested on a present-day machine. In cases with a multi-MA-scale saturated RE current, RE termination is found to be a slow process induced by plasma vertical motion and edge stochasticity,  rather than a rapid collapse driven by intense global MHD instabilities. Such slow termination converts a substantial fraction of the magnetic energy into RE kinetic energy, increasing potential damage to the first wall.
                  </jats:p>

title: Oxide Growth and Recrystallization Behavior of CANDU Zircaloy-4 Cladding during Accelerated Air Oxidation
abstract: Accelerated air oxidation tests were conducted on CANDU spent fuel claddings to determine a practical acceleration criterion for simulated dry-storage specimens. The mechanical integrity of the oxidized cladding was also evaluated after accelerated oxidation. The oxidation tests were performed at 400, 420, and 450 °C in air until oxide layers exceeding 10 μm were formed. Oxide growth, mechanical integrity, and recrystallization behavior were assessed through microstructural characterization, electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD), and ring compression tests (RCT). All conditions successfully generated oxide layers exceeding 10 μm. XRD analysis confirmed predominantly monoclinic ZrO 2 with minor tetragonal ZrO 2 near the oxide/metal interface. RCT results revealed that all oxidized specimens maintained ductility without brittle fracture, indicating that oxidation up to 10 μm did not significantly degrade mechanical integrity. However, recrystallization behavior strongly depended on the oxidation temperature. The as-received microstructure was retained at 400 °C, whereas partial and significant recrystallization occurred at 420 °C and 450 °C, respectively. An EBSD-based time–temperature recrystallization boundary map revealed that recrystallization onset during oxidation to a 10 μm oxide layer occurs at approximately 406 °C. Considering practical uncertainties, 400 °C was determined to be the practical acceleration temperature limit for producing representative simulated dry-storage specimens.

title: Experimental investigation for monitoring axial preload degradation in a scaled-down core support barrel
abstract: The core support barrel (CSB) is continuously forced into lateral motion by the hydraulic load of the incoming coolant and flow-induced vibration (FIV) in the annular downcomer. This motion has been diagnosed via ex-core neutron noise analysis, and the loss of axial preload was identified as the physical factor that relates to the lateral vibration. This loss of preload is primarily attributed to degradation of the hold-down ring and a non-uniform axial preload distribution. In operating nuclear power plants, ex-core neutron noise is monitored through the Internals Vibration Monitoring System (IVMS). However, clear quantitative action criteria have not yet been established. From the perspective of condition monitoring and prognostics, a quantitative index is required to diagnose axial preload variations. In this study, the reduction in axial preload was simulated stepwise on a scaled CSB mock-up that reproduces the load path of the flange fastening region that constitutes the boundary condition of the CSB, and the resulting variations in the first beam mode frequency were investigated by experimental modal analysis (EMA). On this basis, a trend analysis was conducted to monitor the axial preload reduction caused by local and global degradation, through which a monitoring guideline applicable to long-term surveillance was proposed.

title: A Modelica-Based Dynamic Model of a Novel Two-Loop Coupled Configuration for the NHR200-II
abstract: A Modelica-based dynamic model is developed for a novel two-loop configuration of the NHR200-II steam supply system. By eliminating the intermediate isolation loop, the proposed configuration increases saturated steam pressure from 1.6 to 3.2 MPa and temperature from 201.4 to 237.4 °C, while retaining primary-loop natural circulation. The model integrates reactor kinetics, thermal hydraulics, and control components within Modelica's modular, equation-based framework. Steady-state comparisons with design data show a maximum relative deviation of 1.03%. Dynamic comparison with RELAP5 during a 1000 s power reduction from 100% to 50% full power yields root-mean-square deviations of 1.71 °C for core outlet temperature and 0.82 kg/s for steam flow rate, demonstrating consistent transient predictions. Open-loop simulations investigate the coupled neutronic and thermal–hydraulic responses to reactivity insertion, feedwater flow and temperature increases, and steam flow reduction. Closed-loop simulations demonstrate stable load-following operation over 60%–100% full power while maintaining primary-loop natural circulation. The developed model provides a flexible foundation for control strategy development and system-level modeling of nuclear cogeneration and integrated energy applications.

title: Coherent structures and flow periodicities in a mixed-geometry tube array
abstract: U-bend and once-through nuclear steam generators (SG) have tube bundles with highly symmetrical array patterns, typically of square or triangular geometry. The interaction between transverse flows and these spatially periodic tube arrays leads to the formation of coherent flow structures in the form of highly organized vortex shedding in the tube arrays. A consequence of this is potentially damaging vortex-induced vibrations (VIV) resonance. For once-through and U-bend steam generators, VIV is characterized by well-defined Strouhal numbers, which are used to calculate potential VIV resonance frequencies for SG design flow-induced vibration analysis. In helical coil heat exchangers, commonly proposed for compact SMRs designs, the planer tube pattern symmetry is broken. Unlike straight tube bundles, the tube arrangement in each cross-section of a helical coil steam generator is not constant but varies along the helix axis. This mixed-geometry pattern consists of combinations of in-line and parallel triangular tube patterns or even more complex geometries. The present work focuses on the effect of symmetry breaking, in two specific azimuthal planes, by studying the flow in the simplified mixed geometry straight tube arrays, constituted of square and triangular tube configurations. We investigate the flow dynamics effect of interactions between coherent flow structures (modes) from the two constituent sub-arrays. The nonlinear mode interaction leads to bifurcations and creation of new coherent structures or flow modes which are generally more complex in spatial form and spectral content. For the square-triangular hybrid array, the resultant dominant coherent flow mode appears as a modified triangular sub-array mode 1 with additional frequency content associated with mode interaction. The square sub-array mode 1 is significantly suppressed and appears to undergo bifurcation in the mixed geometry array. More generally, the flow behavior in the specific mixed-geometry array studied here suggests that VIV analysis for helical tube bundles is significantly more complex. Unlike the pure symmetric array modes, the mixed-symmetry coherent flow modes show strong non-stationarity with time-variable frequency content. The expected implication for VIV is weaker excitation due to the reduced efficiency of energy transfer to the vibrating tubes.

title: Solid-State Electrolyte Development for Hydrogen Removal from Molten Lithium by Direct LiT Electrolysis
abstract: Direct LiT electrolysis, a tritium extraction process patented at Savannah River National Laboratory (SRNL), utilizes solid-state electrolytes to extract tritium directly from molten Li or PbLi without the need for an extraction solvent. Such a strategy has the potential to reduce the footprint and unit operations of tritium extraction systems in future deuterium-tritium (D-T) fusion power plants. However, optimization of electrolyte properties and an understanding of electrolyte degradation mechanisms are needed to further improve the technological readiness of this process. Here, dense (~97%), single-phase cubic Ta- and Nb-doped lithium lanthanum zirconate (LLZO) electrolytes were synthesized by spark plasma sintering (SPS). Static corrosion testing of Ta-doped LLZO immersed in molten Li at 350°C for 100 h revealed no change in the high Li-ion conductivity cubic garnet LLZO crystal structure. Utilizing a custom impedance testing apparatus, Li-ion conductivities of 6.40 × 10−4 and 2.85 × 10−1 S/cm were measured at room temperature and ~475°C, respectively. Upon exposure to air, an approximately 70% decrease in Li-ion conductivity was observed over ~10.5 h, presumably due to the formation of carbonate species on the LLZO surface. Electrolysis of unpurified Li was conducted with both SPS Ta- and Nb-doped LLZO electrolytes. In both cases, the application of a potential led to large (>500 mA) currents with a clear, concurrent rise in H2 evolution, thereby demonstrating the viability of cubic garnet electrolytes for direct LiT electrolysis. Posttest analysis of the electrolytes showed evidence of dendrite formation growth, and steps to mitigate such phenomena must be considered to improve overall electrolyte durability and lifetime.

title: Ray-Tracing Study of Electron Cyclotron Wave Absorption and Current Drive for Equatorial Port Launchers on EAST
abstract: The electron cyclotron resonance heating (ECRH) and electron cyclotron current drive (ECCD) are investigated by numerical simulation on the Experimental Advanced Superconducting Tokamak (EAST). As a device dedicated to pulse discharge experiments and critical validation for future fusion reactors, EAST requires optimized operational scenarios to enhance heating efficiency. This can be achieved by adjusting the injection angles and launching points of the ECRH launchers, or by shifting the location of the cold resonance layer through controlled variation of the injected electron cyclotron wave frequency or the reference vacuum toroidal magnetic field.However, the propagation of injected electron cyclotron waves may deviate from the intended trajectory due to relativistic effects and Doppler frequency shifts. Moreover, under the present operational conditions of the EAST device, modifications to the reference vacuum toroidal magnetic field are severely constrained by practical engineering limitations. Therefore, it is crucial to assess ECRH and ECCD performance through numerical simulations. This study evaluates the launching points and injection angles of equatorial launchers for a possible 140- to 170-GHz ECRH upgrade, using reference vacuum toroidal fields of 2.5 T and 3 T as selected comparison cases.

title: Conceptual design of an integral scaled facility for the E-SMR concept based on the Power-to-Volume methodology
abstract: Given the growing interest in integral facilities for SMRs to better understand their associated phenomenology and to validate thermal–hydraulic system codes, this work proposes a scaled integral facility for the theoretical E-SMR model from the ELSMOR project. The scaling is based on the Power-to-Volume methodology and constrained by the use of commercially available stainless steel pipes. The exclusion of ad-hoc piping imposes limitations on preserving the scaled volumes, while the chosen methodology does not allow perfect conservation of the prototype’s hydraulic diameters. After analyzing different alternatives, a non-integral facility with separated tubes was selected to better preserve both hydraulic diameters and volumes. Finally, a RELAP5 model of the conceptual scaled facility was developed and compared with the prototype. Simulations of SBO and SB-LOCA events showed that distortions in the scaled coolant volumes, caused by the use of commercial pipes, and in the volumes of structural components lead to deviations in the transient response. A second IET facility was subsequently proposed to address these limitations, resulting in notable improvements in the representativeness of the facility. Nevertheless, considerable distortions in the scaling of the structural components remained, and their impact on the facility response was found to be non-negligible.
title_ko: Power-to-Volume 방법론에 기반한 E-SMR 콘셉트를 위한 통합 축소 시설의 개념 설계

title: The role of different nonlinearities and potential vorticity conservation in two-dimensional fluid ITG models
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The nature of turbulent energy cascade of simple two-dimensional fluid models of ion temperature gradient driven turbulence is studied in detail. Notably, it is observed that a minimal two-field model of toroidal ITG, behaves qualitatively differently with or without the diamagnetic nonlinearity. In its absence, the zonal flows always dominate and the system never reaches a high-transport state. In contrast, when this term is included, zonal flows dominate only near marginality, while away from it, an inverse cascade with high levels of transport is observed, requiring large-scale dissipation (hypoviscosity) to saturate and hyperviscosity to regularize small scale instability associated with this nonlinear term. However introducing such a term, together with the existence of the curvature term, breaks potential vorticity conservation, which is one of the key symmetries of drift-wave turbulence. This can be remedied by considering a more complete model that retains higher-order terms in the pressure equation. This form of the model, with four nonlinearities, conserves potential vorticity and behaves similarly to the original model, requiring hyperviscosity to saturate since the added nonlinearity generates small scale instability also for the pressure equation. To characterize the roles of potential vorticity conservation and higher-order terms in the pressure equation, the behavior of both the standard ITG system, and the potential vorticity conserving system, is studied by analyzing their spectra, turbulent cascades, and sensitivity to viscosity. Finally, the direction of turbulent cascade due to the different nonlinearities is investigated by examining their contributions to the spectral energy transfer and by considering the triadic instability assumption for each of these nonlinearities separately.</jats:p>
title_ko: 2차원 유체 ITG 모델에서 다양한 비선형성과 잠재 와도 보존의 역할

title: The HSX stellarator: History, Design, Construction and Operation
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The Helically Symmetric Experiment (HSX) is a modular stellarator optimized for reduced neoclassical transport. It has a major radius of 1.2 m and an on-axis magnetic field of typically 1 T, and has been operating since 2001. The device distinguishes itself by producing plasmas with fusion relevant electron temperatures well above 1 keV, as well as by providing a comprehensive suite of plasma diagnostics ranging from profile measurements to fluctuation diagnostics. Moreover, as the world's only quasi-helically symmetric device, HSX serves as an important platform for both experimental and numerical studies. In this work, we present an overview of the history, design, construction, and ongoing operation of HSX, with the goal of establishing a reference and informing the design of future stellarator experiments.</jats:p>
title_ko: HSX 스텔러레이터: 역사, 설계, 건설 및 운영

title: Outcomes of activation measurements and analyses of ITER materials during JET DTE3 operations
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The 2023 JET deuterium-tritium (D--T) experimental campaign (DTE3) achieved record fusion energy output (69 MJ), providing a unique 14.1~MeV neutron environment for irradiation studies. A range of ITER material samples were exposed in a Long-Term Irradiation Station (LTIS) within the JET nuclear environment to neutron fluxes up to $2 \times 10^{13}$~n/cm$^{2}$/s, reaching a total neutron fluence of $7 \times 10^{15}$~n/cm$^{2}$, the highest achieved in a tokamak. Post-irradiation analysis using high-resolution gamma spectrometry across five laboratories identified a range of neutron-induced activation products present in these samples, which were quantitatively compared with neutronics simulation predictions. Complementary neutron fluence measurements with metallic dosimetry foils located in the LTIS enabled validation of the simulation approach via MCNP and FISPACT-II codes. The DTE3 campaign results, combined with those obtained from prior D--T campaigns, provide a highly valuable dataset for ITER and other D--T machines, supporting the validation of predictive nuclear modelling tools towards sustained high power D--T operations.</jats:p>
title_ko: JET DTE3 운영 중 ITER 재료에 대한 활성화 측정 및 분석 결과

title: Modeling of turbulent transport by dissipative trapped electron mode in tokamak plasmas
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This work develops reduced turbulent transport&#xD;models for laboratory plasmas in toroidal devices by gyrokinetic analyses.&#xD; The turbulent transport in the relatively collisional plasmas studied in this article &#xD;is excited by the dissipative trapped electron mode (d-TEM) &#xD; and the ion temperature gradient (ITG) mode.&#xD; Linear analysis is performed to determine the linear growth rate &#xD; and a characteristic quantity of the zonal-flow linear response, namely the zonal flow decay time.&#xD;Reduced models for the d-TEM/ITG modes are constructed &#xD;from linear quantities related to the mixing-length estimate &#xD;and the zonal flow decay time.&#xD;The reduced models reproduce the nonlinear gyrokinetic simulation results for turbulent transport.&#xD;The diffusivity models and the quasilinear flux models are proposed for the reduced models.&#xD;The effect of zonal flows on turbulent transport is studied for the d-TEM/ITG plasmas.</jats:p>

title: Incorporating soft X-ray measurements for MHD equilibrium reconstructions of Wendelstein 7-X plasmas
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Three-dimensional reconstructions of Wendelstein 7-X (W7-X) equilibria incorporating soft X-ray measurements are presented. The STELLOPT code [2] has been enhanced to include soft X-ray measurements, complementing the set of diagnostics accessible for equilibrium search. The approach is based on the alignment of radiation strength with magnetic flux surfaces, which is justified for&#xD;most W7-X plasmas. The emissivity reconstruction works reliably and reproduces measurements within the expected range of uncertainty. Results are in line with independent tomographic inversion methods for calculating radiation patterns, offering an alternative way of analyzing the soft X-ray signals. A comparison of the magnetic axis shift found in the equilibria as well as the tomograms shows overall agreement. The methods are demonstrated for three W7-X experimental programs, covering different magnetic field configurations and plasma parameters, including high performance plasma cases with volume averaged plasma beta of up to 2 %, central beta of up to 7 % and magnetic axis shift of up to 12 cm. For these experiments, the standard W7-X diagnostic set constrains the flux-surface geometry in the equilibrium reconstruction to an accuracy of about 6 mm.</jats:p>
title_ko: 웬델슈타인 7-X 플라즈마의 MHD 평형 재구성(equilibrium reconstruction)을 위한 연X선 측정 통합

title: Experimental Study of Thermal Radiation in a Large PANDA Vessel with Steam Content Variation
abstract: In this paper, we present an experimental investigation of thermal radiation effects in the PANDA facility (Paul Scherrer Institute, Switzerland), focusing on gas atmospheres with different steam content. Thermal radiation may influence the containment atmosphere temperature and buoyancy, thereby affecting hydrogen distribution during a postulated accident. Two new experiments at initial steam contents of 5% and 30% extend the previously published HYMERES-2 measurements, filling the remaining steam-content gap. The combined dataset comprises five experiments from the OECD/NEA PANDA-1 and HYMERES-2 projects, spanning 0.1% to 60% steam. Particular attention is given to quantifying the post-compression thermal relaxation across this extended range.The containment atmosphere initially consisted of an air and steam mixture at elevated temperature, except for the nearly dry reference experiment, which started at room temperature. A helium-rich layer was established in the upper region to limit convective mixing induced by the subsequent helium injection. Its nominal initial helium concentration was 50%, except in the 30% steam experiment, where it was approximately 100%. The gas mixture was compressed by injecting helium at 10 g/s from the top over 1 200 s. The subsequent gas thermal behavior and concentration distribution were recorded during the compression phase and a 1 800-s decay phase.Higher initial steam contents were associated with lower peak excess temperatures and faster thermal relaxation. Using a common temperature-based criterion for the return toward the initial thermal state, the experiments with 2%, 5%, and 60% steam reached this condition 950, 860, and 540 s after injection stopped, respectively. The nearly dry reference did not reach it during the observation period. The 30% steam experiment reached the criterion after 400 s. These findings have profound implications for computational fluid dynamics calculations in the presence of steam.
title_ko: 증기 함량 변화가 있는 대형 PANDA 용기 내 열복사에 대한 실험적 연구

title: Influence of Fe-Ion-induced displacement damage on deuterium retention and plasma-induced surface degradation of detonation-sprayed tungsten coating
abstract: Tungsten-based materials are considered leading candidates for plasma-facing components in future fusion reactors, where irradiation-induced defects can significantly affect hydrogen isotope retention and surface stability. In this work, the influence of 3.5 MeV Fe-ion pre-damage on deuterium (D) plasma-induced surface modification and D retention was investigated in detonation-sprayed tungsten (DS-W) coatings. The effects of exposure temperature (500, 650, and 800 K) and D fluence (1 × 10 24 , 5 × 10 24 , 1 × 10 25 D/m 2 ) were systematically investigated for DS-W. A comparative assessment of atmospheric plasma-sprayed tungsten (APS-W) and pure tungsten (PW) was also conducted at 500 K and a D fluence of 1 × 10 25 D/m 2 . The samples were pre-irradiated with 3.5 MeV Fe-ions to a maximum damage level of approximately 0.9 dpa and subsequently exposed to 40 eV/D plasma. The results showed that Fe-ion pre-damage enhanced D retention in DS-W by introducing additional irradiation-induced trapping sites. Surface degradation in DS-W increased with increasing D fluence but decreased with increasing exposure temperature, owing to enhanced D diffusion and thermal release. Correspondingly, D retention decreased progressively from 500 to 800 K, while Fe-ion pre-damaged samples consistently retained more D than un-damaged samples. At 500 K, APS-W exhibited the most severe surface degradation and the highest D retention, followed by DS-W, whereas PW exhibited slightly lower D retention and better resistance to plasma-induced surface damage. These results demonstrated that both irradiation-induced defects and intrinsic microstructural characteristics played key roles in governing D trapping and retention in tungsten-based plasma-facing materials.
title_ko: Fe 이온 유도 전위 손상이 중수소 보유 및 폭발 분사 텅스텐 코팅의 플라즈마 유도 표면 열화에 미치는 영향

title: In-situ tritium release experiments using Li2TiO3 pebbles fabricated by an emulsion process for Q-DEMO activities
abstract: In–situ tritium release experiments using Li 2 TiO 3 pebbles are essential for understanding tritium residence time and the chemical forms of released species. The tritium release behavior of Li 2 TiO 3 is known to vary significantly depending on fabrication–induced characteristics such as grain size and density. This study reports the preparatory status and initial results of in–situ tritium release experiments using Li 2 TiO 3 pebbles fabricated by an emulsion process for Q–DEMO activities. A dedicated irradiation rig and tritium detection system were developed to separately measure HT (T 2 ) and HTO (T 2 O), supported by neutron transport and thermophysical analyses. Preliminary results obtained at low temperatures (400–600 °C) are presented.

title: Optimized finite-β tokamak-stellarator hybrid configurations achieved by planar dipole-field coils
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Tokamak--stellarator hybrids seek to combine tokamak-like compactness and confinement with stellarator-like externally generated rotational transform and steady-state operation. In this work, we build on the recent tokamak--stellarator hybrid study using planar dipole-field coils (PDCs) [Yu et al., arXiv:2605.03599], in which the fixed-position, programmable coils on an axisymmetric winding surface generate flexible three-dimensional shaping fields. Using single-stage free-boundary optimization of coil currents and plasma-equilibrium parameters, we construct vacuum and finite-β configurations. The vacuum cases show controllable external transform and magnetic well.&#xD;The finite-β cases accommodate various density, temperature, and pressure profiles, producing quasi-axisymmetric (QA) equilibria with self-consistent bootstrap current, favorable Mercier stability, and reduced demand for external current drive. Re-optimization enables β ramp-up and access to different field-period QA branches with moderate coil-current changes. At large rotational transform, a toroidally omnigenous (TO)-like configuration exhibits more favorable infinite-n ideal-ballooning behavior than a QA reference with matched profiles, even though ballooning stability is not directly optimized for. These results demonstrate that PDCs provide a flexible platform for achieving optimized finite-β hybrid configurations.</jats:p>

title: Nitrogen-seeded X-point radiator regime with good core-edge compatibility and reduced divertor in-out asymmetry in WEST L-mode plasmas
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The X-point radiator (XPR) regime is considered a promising approach for mitigating divertor heat flux during long-pulse operation. In this work, nitrogen-seeded XPR discharges are investigated in WEST L-mode plasmas with a full-tungsten environment and an ITER-grade divertor. The XPR transition is characterized by an increase followed by a rapid decrease in the line-integrated density near the X-point, together with an abrupt collapse of the electron temperature at the outer strike point. During the XPR phase, both divertor targets remain detached with electron temperatures of about 3 eV and strongly reduced heat fluxes. Analysis of multiple XPR discharges shows that the plasma stored energy increases after nitrogen seeding and remains elevated throughout the XPR phase, accompanied by higher core temperature and/or density, indicating good core-edge compatibility. During the XPR phase, the total radiated power increases, with a larger fraction of the radiation originating from the X-point region, while tungsten sputtering at the divertor targets and the tungsten content in the core plasma are reduced. The pronounced in-out asymmetry of divertor plasma parameters observed in conventional discharges is also reduced. SOLEDGE3X simulations reproduce the experimental observations and suggest that the reduced in-out asymmetry is associated with reduced ionization and more similar poloidal deuterium ion transport on the inner and outer divertor legs.</jats:p>
title_ko: WEST L-모드 플라즈마에서 양호한 코어-에지(core-edge) 호환성과 감소된 다이버터 인-아웃(in-out) 비대칭성을 갖는 질소 시드 X-포인트 방사체 체제

title: Machine learning for classification, dimension reduction, clustering, and feature importance analysis of QH-mode plasma regimes
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Edge-localized modes (ELMs) release bursts of energy and particles that threaten plasma-facing components in future tokamak reactors, making ELM-free operating regimes a priority for fusion research. Quiescent H-mode (QH), wide-pedestal QH-mode (WPQH), and broadband QH-mode (BBQH) form a family of ELM-free regimes at DIII-D whose boundaries and controlling parameters remain incompletely understood. This work aims to identify, from data, which measured quantities distinguish the three regimes, using a physics-labeled database of 482 high-confidence segments drawn from 323 DIII-D discharges, whose manual labeling was accelerated by the Data Fusion Labeler (dFL). An XGBoost classifier trained on 1 ms-resolution diagnostic data establishes that the manual labels are learnable: under leave-one-shot-out cross-validation it reproduces them for 87.3% of 1 ms samples (macro-F1 0.82). The same classifier underpins dFL's autolabeler for extending the database across the archive, at an estimated ~50× speedup over fully manual analysis. A supervised feature-importance analysis (classifiers evaluated on held-out discharges, with SHAP attribution), trained only on physics signals not used as labeling criteria, shows that the regimes are also distinguishable from independent physics quantities, and unsupervised dimension-reduction and clustering methods examine the same data without labels. The analysis recovers injected torque as the dominant actuator distinguishing the regimes. Within the rotation and E_r quantities considered, edge E×B shear carries the most information distinguishing the three regimes, while toroidal rotation also contributes strongly; this is a statistical association for this model and dataset, consistent with the critical-shear picture of edge harmonic oscillation onset. Where the supervised and unsupervised rankings appear to disagree, the disagreement reflects the correlation structure among related features rather than a substantive physics dispute. Together, these results identify key physical quantities associated with QH-mode regime boundaries and provide a reusable, interpretable workflow for machine-learning-based analysis of labeled databases in fusion research.</jats:p>
title_ko: QH-모드 플라즈마 모드의 분류, 차원 축소, 클러스터링 및 특성 중요도 분석을 위한 머신 러닝

title: Implementation and first application of EMC3-EIRENE on DTT for assessing the heat load on the ICRH antenna
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This paper reports on the implementation process of the three-dimensional (3D) edge plasma transport code EMC3-EIRENE on the Divertor Tokamak Test (DTT) facility and the results of its first application, with a focus on assessing the heat load on the Ion Cyclotron Resonance Heating (ICRH) antenna surfaces. The full 3D ICRH antenna structure is incorporated in the 3D simulations. Assuming different toroidal symmetry for the antenna to determine whether the heat load assessment can be carried out with reduced computational effort, and to what extent a 3D assessment deviates. The predictions of the 3D antenna heat load distribution are obtained and the peak values on the top plate and the two side plates reach 0.9, 2.1 and 3.8 MW/m², respectively. The scan of transport coefficients reveals that the heat load was mainly influenced by the plasma density. Increasing the transport coefficients could lead to a corresponding increase in the heat load up to 1-2 order of magnitude. 3D gas puffing is included to evaluate its impact on the antenna heat load. It can increase the local plasma density near the antenna, potentially raising the heat load on the antenna surfaces by a factor of 2–3. The corresponding 3D edge plasma behavior is presented under the coupled effects of gas puffing and the antenna geometrical structure.</jats:p>
title_ko: ICRH 안테나의 열 부하를 평가하기 위한 DTT에 대한 EMC3-EIRENE의 구현 및 최초 적용

title: Impacts of energetic ion on the unstable spectra of kinetic ballooning modes and zonal flow generation
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Global gyrokinetic particle simulations are employed to investigate the interaction between energetic ions (EIs) and kinetic ballooning modes (KBMs) across different toroidal mode number ($n$) regimes, encompassing linear dispersion relations, nonlinear wave-particle interactions, and wave-wave interactions. The results demonstrate that EIs exert non-perturbative destabilizing effects on low-$n$ KBMs, while stabilizing high-$n$ KBMs through thermal ion dilution. These opposing EI effects arise from the different strengths of finite Larmor radius (FLR) and finite orbit width (FOW) effects in low- and high-$n$ regimes. Single-$n$ and multi-$n$ nonlinear simulations reveal strong wave-particle interactions between EIs and low-$n$ KBMs, resulting in higher KBM saturation levels and enhanced EI transport. Additionally, although low-density EIs have little direct influence on zonal flow (ZF), they can indirectly increase the spatial scale of ZF in multi-$n$ simulations. Since ZF is generated via the beat‑driven process and its structure is determined by the pump wave, the EI effects lead to the dominance of low‑$n$ KBM components, thereby increasing the spatial scale of the ZF.</jats:p>

title: Hybrid simulations of nonlinear zonal flow generation by multi-n toroidal Alfvén eigenmodes driven by energetic particles
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In burning plasmas, zonal flows (ZFs) excited by toroidal Alfvén eigenmodes (TAEs) play a crucial role in improving energy confinement. In this work, strong self-generated ZFs are analyzed in a multi-n TAE system through nonlinear hybrid simulations using the CLT-K code, where the ZFs are driven by self-beat interactions of TAEs. The results show that the strong ZFs dominate the nonlinear stage and significantly suppress the TAE activity. The ZF mode structures consist of the m=0 and m=1 harmonics, and are directly correlated with the spatial structures of TAEs. Further analysis of the ZF kinetic energy evolution demonstrates that a finite residual between the Reynolds and Maxwell stresses, arising from toroidal geometry, enables net energy transfer from TAEs to ZFs, with an additional contribution from the EP pressure response. In addition, the linear Lorentz force contributes either to ZF pumping or damping depending on the stage of the evolution. Strong ZF generation is favored in regimes with high EP pressure and low viscosity. A self-regulating process is identified: stronger TAEs drive stronger ZFs, which in turn regulates the TAE activity. These findings provide both numerical and physical insights into the role of ZFs in regulating EP-driven instabilities in tokamak plasmas.</jats:p>

title: Grain boundary effects on surface modifications of tungsten under fusion-relevant helium plasma irradiation: Coarse-grained vs. Nano-grained microstructures
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Grain refinement is widely regarded as an effective strategy for improving radiation resistance in nuclear materials, but the influence of grain boundaries (GBs) on helium (He) plasma irradiation-induced surface modifications in tungsten (W) remains unclear. Here, we compare the surface morphology evolution and subsurface bubble distributions of coarse-grained and nano-grained W under fusion-relevant He plasma irradiation. The samples were exposed simultaneously to 90 eV He ions at 1173 K. Although both microstructures ultimately developed similar fuzz composed of nanoscale tendrils, their early-stage evolution of surface roughening exhibited distinct differences. In the nano-grained W film, ~600 nm thick, surface roughening was initiated by anomalous bubble growth at grain junctions. In contrast, coarse-grained W exhibited pronounced crystallographic-orientation-dependent roughening. Subsequent tendril nucleation and growth occurred in both microstructures, preferentially at highly convex surface regions. Moreover, subsurface bubbles were confined mainly to a shallow region approximately 100–200 nm beneath coarse-grained W, whereas they permeated the entire nano-grained film. These results indicate that GB-mediated bubble dynamics primarily govern surface evolution during the fuzz-incubation stage, while interface curvature and capillary-driven diffusion dominate tendril nucleation and subsequent growth. Thus, GBs exert a decisive influence during early-stage surface roughening but have limited effect on the later development of fuzz. These findings provide insight into the distinct and common mechanisms governing He-induced surface modification in W with different grain sizes and support a capillary-growth framework for fuzz formation.</jats:p>

title: Augmenting the extrapolation capability of disruption prediction to extended parameter regimes by predict-first neural network
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The prediction, mitigation, and avoidance of disruptions are critical prerequisites for ensuring the safe operation of future fusion reactors. While machine learning-based disruption prediction techniques have achieved high accuracy in recent years, their application to a new device demands strong extrapolation capability across parameter regimes. This capability is essential to maintain robust algorithm performance as the operational space of the device expands, while it is also a main shortcoming for most machine learning techniques. This study evaluates the extrapolation capability of a disruption prediction algorithm using multiple subsets of experimental data from HL-3 tokamak, divided by key plasma parameters, yielding three key findings. Firstly, the area under the receiver-operator characteristic curve (AUC) of a standard deep learning algorithm trained on the subset with low parameters degrades to around 0.750, 0.666, and 0.540 when extrapolated to three progressively distant extrapolation regimes. However, the Predict-First Neural Network (PFNN) maintains an AUC of about 0.873, 0.823 and 0.701. Secondly, the algorithm's accuracy shows a clear contrast in degradation behavior: when extrapolating along electromagnetic parameters like plasma current, performance declines slowly and continuously; when extrapolating along energy-related parameters like stored energy, performance remains initially stable but deteriorates abruptly beyond a certain threshold. Finally, after rigorously accounting for the impact of parameter regime extrapolation and adjusting the algorithm deployment strategy, deep learning proved effective in protecting the device during HL-3's high-current and high-beta commissioning phases. This study provides valuable experience for implementing disruption prediction algorithms on new devices and is expected to offer practical reference for the initial operation of future fusion facilities like ITER.</jats:p>

title: Nuclear Energy Perceptions among Predominantly Urban and Highly Educated Respondents in Malaysia: Policy Implications in the Context of the 13th Malaysia Plan
abstract: Malaysia’s rising energy demand and net-zero target by 2050 have renewed interest in nuclear power as a low-carbon option under the Thirteenth Malaysia Plan (RMK-13). This study assessed nuclear energy knowledge, perceptions, and support among 400 Malaysian adults recruited through an online non-probability convenience survey. The sample was predominantly urban and highly educated; the findings should not be interpreted as nationally representative. Data were analyzed descriptively and inferentially using Microsoft Excel. The 15-items knowledge assessment indicate that respondents showed reasonable understanding of the basic functions, applications, and operational safety of nuclear energy with 94.3% recognized nuclear power as an alternative electricity source and 79.5% knew that Malaysia has research reactors rather than commercial nuclear power plants. However, 45.8% were unsure or confused about the relationship between nuclear plants and nuclear bombs. Reported dimension means were highest for policy and governance (3.97), followed by the environment (3.76), economy (3.57), and safety (3.55). The overall support mean was 3.83, and 83.8% supported exploring nuclear energy under RMK-13. Support differed significantly by gender (p < 0.001) and education level (p = 0.002). Favorable support scores coexisted with concerns about safety, transparency, and siting in the open-ended responses.

title: Machine-learning-accelerated multi-objective optimization of forward-directed neutron sources via Geant4 simulations
abstract: Designing compact, forward-directed neutron sources requires navigating a vast parameter space. Yield, directionality, and energy often compete, making this a multi-objective challenge that has resisted systematic optimization. We present a machine-learning-accelerated framework that addresses this problem by combining large-scale Geant4 Monte Carlo simulations with a feed-forward neural network emulator and SHAP interpretability analysis. We construct a dataset of 2880 simulated reaction configurations spanning stable beam and target isotopes from hydrogen to aluminum, with 100 million primary ions per configuration. The trained emulator rapidly predicts two figures of merit: the forward neutron flux within a zero-to-fifteen-degree cone about the beam axis, and the corresponding mean neutron energy. Multi-objective optimization over the emulator identifies a Pareto-optimal front that delineates the best attainable trade-offs between these competing objectives. SHAP analysis reveals that beam ions and their energies are the dominant performance drivers. Deuterium beams paired with low-Z targets—such as 6 Li, 7 Li, and 9 Be—consistently populate the Pareto front. Target density, by contrast, exerts comparatively little independent influence. Notably, the emulator achieves its highest accuracy in the region of objective space most relevant to the application: errors are concentrated among configurations with low flux and low energy, which are less desirable by design. Because Geant4 is known to underestimate thick-target neutron yields for certain channels, the reported Pareto-optimal fluxes represent conservative lower bounds. The workflow establishes a general, extensible template for simulation-to-ML neutron source optimization. It also provides a quantitative roadmap for guiding targeted experimental validation.

title: Does information framing matter for nuclear waste acceptance? An experimental test of social comparison, urgency, and intergenerational equity frames
abstract: Public acceptance is a precondition for siting a high-level radioactive waste (HLRW) repository, yet experimental evidence on how disposal information should be communicated is scarce, particularly in East Asia. This study tests whether three theoretically distinct information frames — a precedent from an advanced country, the projected saturation of domestic on-site storage facilities, and the intergenerational burden of unmanaged waste — produce different levels of acceptance of HLRW repository construction in South Korea. A between-subjects experiment with pre- and post-treatment measurement was embedded in a national web survey of Korean adults with quotas matched on region, gender, and age (N = 1,898). Acceptance, perceived risk, perceived benefit, knowledge, and negative affective imagery were measured, and pre–post differences and between-frame contrasts were analyzed using confidence intervals, equivalence tests, and multiple regression. Because the pre- and post-treatment items used different response formats (5-point and 7-point), raw change scores confound genuine attitude change with the mechanical expansion of the response range. On a common 0–100 metric, the average shift was small and slightly negative (−0.84 points, 95% CI [−1.66, −0.02]), while the proportion of supportive respondents increased by 1.0 to 4.0 percentage points. The randomized between-frame comparison, which is unaffected by the change in response format, yields differences of at most 0.06 scale points, with 90% confidence intervals contained well within an equivalence bound of d = 0.20. Perceived benefit is the strongest condition-general predictor of acceptance and of the raw pre–post difference scores, followed by knowledge, whereas perceived risk and negative affective imagery are weak or null. Condition-specific change-score regressions suggest different correlational patterns across the three frames, although the response-format mismatch limits their interpretation as persuasion pathways. The particular frame adopted by a credible message appears to matter far less than the message’s substantive content, but the design does not support strong claims about the magnitude of information-induced attitude change.

title: Cost-informed selection of the lower bound of the gray region in MARSSIM final status survey planning
abstract: Background In MARSSIM Final Status Survey (FSS) planning, the Lower Bound of the Gray Region (LBGR) is often treated as a fixed statistical input, although it also affects remediation burden and survey cost. Methods This study formulates LBGR as a cost-statistical decision variable. For each candidate LBGR, the method calculates relative shift, required FSS sample size, remediation steps, remediation cost, and FSS cost, and selects the feasible candidate with the minimum total cost. A three-regime analysis further evaluates how the initial contamination level relative to DCGL W changes the decision between mandatory remediation, additional remediation, and sampling-only planning. Results In the hypothetical baseline case, the optimized LBGR was approximately 150.0 Bq/g, requiring 15 samples and two remediation steps, with a total cost of approximately 142,500 USD. Sensitivity analyses showed that beta relaxation reduces sample size at the cost of greater Type II error tolerance, whereas sigma reduction changes both sample size and the selected cleanup target. The sample-size calculation was checked against a published MARSSIM example. Conclusion The framework provides a transparent basis for balancing cost, statistical conservatism, data quality, and regulatory defensibility in FSS planning.

title: Reassessing double-ended guillotine break requirements: evidence-based analysis of regulatory assumptions after five decades of nuclear operation
abstract: Nuclear power plant regulations mandate comprehensive protection against the postulated double-ended guillotine break (DEGB) scenarios, involving the instantaneous, complete circumferential severance of the largest reactor-coolant system piping. The DEGB is the largest possible pipe break and it is encompassed by a large break loss of coolant (LBLOCA) accident postulated as a design basis accident for large water reactor nuclear power plants by the U.S. nuclear regulatory guidance. Despite more than 20,000 reactor-years of cumulative global operating experience spanning 35 countries and over 650 reactors that have operated historically, including units that have subsequently been permanently shut down, zero DEGB events have been documented in any domestic or international reporting system. This paper examines the technical, probabilistic, and materials-science evidence underlying the DEGB postulate and evaluates whether it continues to be an appropriate design-basis assumption. Probabilistic fracture-mechanics analyses—including studies commissioned directly by the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC)—consistently place direct crack-induced DEGB frequencies on the order of 10 −12 per reactor-year, and seismically induced pathways yield frequencies of 10 −7 to 10 −6 per reactor-year, well below thresholds conventionally used to define credible design-basis events. Ductile nuclear piping materials exhibit stable crack-growth behavior that is mechanistically incompatible with instantaneous circumferential severance. International regulatory experience—particularly Germany's four decade implementation of break preclusion and the NRC's approval of leak-before-break methodology for nearly all U.S. pressurized-water reactors—validates that alternatives to DEGB protection maintain safety while significantly reducing economic burden. Current DEGB-driven protection systems impose estimated costs of hundreds of millions of dollars per plant, with fleetwide and global aggregate impacts reaching tens of billions of dollars. This paper demonstrates that the evidence base accumulated over five decades is sufficient to justify removing DEGB from design-basis requirements through formal rulemaking, rather than continuing the current case-by-case exemption approach, and also provides a framework for risk-informed implementation consistent with modern regulatory standards.

title: Variable Suction Impact on Transient EMHD Thermospecies Transport Through Accelerated Boundary Layers
abstract: A comprehensive numerical approach towards modeling the impact of variable suction on a electrically conducting magneto-hydrodynamic (MHD) fluid passing through a permeable media supporting convection naturally is investigated in this paper. The fluid under consideration is a casson fluid whose key characteristics include electrical conductivity, viscosity, incompressibility, and mass diffusivity. Although the fluid is non-Newtonian, with extremely higher values for the casson parameter, the fluid behaves as Newtonian.A highly stable finite difference scheme is employed to solve the model. The fluid momentum, energy, and solute diffusivity, along with skin friction, Nusselt number, and Sherwood number, are the significant fundamental properties studied in this paper. The critical flow parameters are comprised the electromagnetic field, permeability, and suction parameter.The visualizations revealed that a significant enhancement in the suction parameter results in considerable deterioration of the thermal and mass transfer along with the flow profile. Unique combinations of the electromagnetic effect with the Prandtl number and external heating that suppresses the fluid motion add to the novelty of this study. The unique interplay between the parameters contributes insights effortlessly to liquid-metal fusion blankets, tokamak cores, laboratory surrogate experiments, and many more fusion science concepts.

title: Understanding of Quasi-Coherent Fluctuations in Tokamaks Through Diagnostics and Analysis: A Review
abstract: This paper presents a review of experimental studies on quasi-coherent fluctuations (QCFs) in tokamaks. The research focuses on the analysis of plasma turbulence characteristics measured using various diagnostic systems: collective Bragg scattering, heavy ion beam probe, beam emission spectroscopy, Langmuir probes, and correlation reflectometry. The study examines the properties of quasi-coherent oscillations observed predominantly in the frequency range around 100 kHz. The paper discusses the main parameters of these fluctuations: wave numbers, phase velocities, coherence degree, and their spatial distribution in the plasma column. Special attention is paid to the comparison of measurement results obtained using different diagnostic methods and the analysis of discrepancies between them. The work analyzes the problem of transition between reference frames (laboratory and plasma frames) and its impact on the interpretation of experimental data. The influence of plasma rotation and E×B drift on the observed characteristics of fluctuations is considered. The paper also discusses the limitations and advantages of various diagnostic techniques in studying plasma turbulence. The results show that QCFs exhibit enhanced coherence and appear as burstlike events in specific tokamak operating regimes. These fluctuations affect particle and energy transport in the plasma, making their study crucial for understanding turbulence in magnetic confinement devices. The paper highlights the need for further research to develop theoretical research studies explaining all aspects of QCF behavior.

title: Sensitivity of Shutdown Dose Rates to Irradiation History Assumptions
abstract: An accurate prediction of shutdown dose rates (SDRs) in fusion systems depends on assumptions made regarding irradiation history. In activation and depletion calculations, irradiation schedules are represented using discrete time steps, and high-fidelity pulsed operation may require many time steps to resolve radionuclide buildup and decay. To reduce the computational requirements, which are directly proportional to the number of time steps, irradiation histories are often simplified through time step coarsening, which effectively combines smaller time steps into fewer but larger “effective” time steps; however, the impact of these simplifications on SDRs needs to be better understood.This work investigates the sensitivity of SDR predictions to irradiation schedule simplifications using an OpenMC-based R2S (rigorous two-step) methodology applied to a representative MAST-U (Mega Ampere Spherical Tokamak Upgrade) irradiation environment. A detailed pulsed irradiation schedule is compared against progressively coarsened schedules while maintaining consistent geometry, materials, and neutron source normalization. The results show that time step coarsening produces the largest differences immediately after shutdown, where short-lived radionuclides strongly influence activation behavior. At longer cooling times, SDR predictions converge as long-lived radionuclides dominate and activation becomes governed primarily by total neutron fluence rather than irradiation schedule resolution. These findings help identify when irradiation schedule simplifications may be adequate for SDR assessments in fusion systems.

title: Effect of Cooling Pipe Diameter on Tritium Production Distribution in a Water-Cooled Blanket for a DEMO Reactor
abstract: Demonstration fusion reactor (DEMO) will aim to fulfill the tritium self-sufficiency in fuel recycling and generate economical fusion energy in the future. Tritium self-sufficiency is one of the key requirements for future fusion reactors. In water-cooled solid breeder blankets, the cooling-channel geometry affects neutron moderation and consequently influences the spatial distribution of tritium breeding. This study quantitatively evaluates the effect of cooling pipe diameter on near-pipe tritium accumulation and tritium release potential in a PWR water-cooled solid breeder blanket. Five cooling pipe diameters, 5.6, 7.5, 9.3, 11.3, and 13.8 mm, are considered using local tritium production densities extracted at positions far from and close to the cooling pipe. Three indicators are introduced, the tritium production density difference, the near-pipe enhancement ratio, and the tritium accumulation factor. The results show that as the cooling pipe diameter increases from 5.6 to 13.8 mm, the near-pipe tritium production density increases from 1.37 × 1013 to 1.88 × 1013 n × s−1 × cm−3, whereas the far-pipe value changes only slightly from 1.26 × 1013 to 1.32 × 1013 n × s−1 × cm−3. The enhancement ratio increases from 8.7% to 42.4%, and the accumulation factor increases from 1.087 to 1.424. These results indicate that increasing the cooling pipe diameter mainly intensifies local tritium accumulation in the low-temperature region around the cooling pipe rather than uniformly increasing tritium production throughout the breeder zone. Therefore, cooling pipe diameter optimization should consider heat removal, tritium breeding performance, and tritium release potential simultaneously.

title: A Small-Scale High-Temperature Furnace for Gas-Atomization of Novel Reduced-Activation Copper Alloys
abstract: A compact, high-temperature tube furnace capable of 1 800°C continuous operation was designed for novel alloy development and integrated within a small-scale gas atomizer. Off-the-shelf components minimized machining and enabled construction for less than ~$8 000. A hollow carbon arc gouging electrode acting as the furnace tube was heated by an axial current flow. Reaction rates between the carbon tube body and the Cu-Ti, Cr alloys occurr at much longer timescales than the 6-min alloy melt time, mitigating reactions with metal alloys.Water-cooled end-cap electrodes on opposing ends of a 2.75-deg ConFlat cross and forced air cool the furnace envelope. PAN (polyacrylonitrile) graphite felt insulation within the furnace envelope reduced radiative heat loss, while an argon gas purge preventeds oxidation. The low-cost carbon tube enabled replacement between runs to eliminate material cross contamination.A PID (proportional-integral-derivative) feedback control stabilized the carbon tube temperature, which was measured by a two-color pyrometer within a steady-state error of <0.5°C and achieved a rise time to 1 800°C of under 20 s. Intermittent operation at 2 360°C with 1 810 W of heating power was limited by the degradation of the Viton O-rings and the pyrometer measurement range.Axial thermocouple measurements indicated an 80-mm-long section of uniform temperature. A pulsed argon feed ejected the molten alloy melt from the furnace into the associated gas atomizer. Scanning electron microscopy/energy dispersive Xr-ay analyses of the powders from test melts indicated a consistent distribution of the solute elements within the individual gas-atomized powder particles for the Cu-V-Ta, Cu-Cr-Ti, and Cu-Cr-Ta alloys produced at 1 800°C for 6 min.

title: Thermocouple layout optimisation towards divertor digital twins using Bayesian experimental design
abstract: Divertor thermocouples can provide robust, in-vessel monitoring of heat loads during short attached or reattachment phases, but their number and accessible locations are limited. We present a Bayesian experimental design workflow to optimise thermocouple placement applied to MAST Upgrade (MAST-U) divertor tiles 3 and 4 for conventional and elongated magnetic configurations. A maximum-entropy design in heat flux decay length ( λ q ), Gaussian spreading width ( S ) and scrape-off-layer power ( P S O L ) generates a representative ensemble of attached plasma states spanning configuration-specific parameter ranges and strike-point locations ( R s p , Z s p ). For each state we compute synthetic thermocouple readings using the Heat Flux Engineering Analysis Toolkit and OpenFOAM. A Gaussian process surrogate, coupled to digiLab’s Bayesian experimental designer in the Uncertainty Engine, selects sensor subsets (1–10 sensors) that maximise expected information gain on quantities of interest θ = ( λ q , S , P S O L , R s p , Z s p ) . The resulting designs concentrate around the strike region while retaining off-peak coverage to resolve profile shape, and exhibit clear diminishing returns with increasing sensor count. This provides quantitative, configuration-specific layouts for MAST-U tiles 3 and 4 as a case study, with a transferable methodology for diagnostics design in future divertor-equipped devices and power plants.
